desc:
Given a lowercase string s and an integer k, count the substrings of s that have length exactly k and in which all characters are different. Substrings are counted by their start position, so equal substrings found at different places each count.

s = "abcabcbb", k = 3
windows: abc bca cab abc bcb cbb
valid:   yes yes yes yes no  no
result = 4

If k is larger than 26, no window can have all-different letters, so the answer is 0.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Putting every window into a set and comparing the set size with k works, but costs O(n · k).
Consecutive windows share k - 1 characters. Keep character counts and update them by adding the new letter and removing the old one.
Track how many letters currently have a count of 2 or more. The window is valid exactly when that number is zero.
editorial: Slide a window of length k across the string while keeping a count per letter and a variable repeats that holds the number of letters whose count is at least 2. When a letter is added and its count becomes 2, increase repeats; when a letter is removed and its count drops from 2 to 1, decrease it.

After each step the window has length k; if repeats is 0, every letter in it is different and we count it. Every character enters and leaves the window once, so the time is O(n) and the extra memory is O(1) (26 counters). Rebuilding a set for each window would cost O(n · k).
